basic_information.name: Microsoft Agent Framework (Semantic Kernel + AutoGen)
basic_information.creator: Microsoft (Semantic Kernel team + Microsoft Research AutoGen team, unified under the Microsoft Foundry organization)
basic_information.release_date: October 1, 2025 (public preview); Semantic Kernel originally released March 2023, AutoGen originally released September 2023. The Agent Framework merges both into a single unified SDK.
basic_information.current_version: Public Preview (as of February 2026); GA 1.0 targeted end of Q1 2026. Semantic Kernel latest: v1.70.0 (.NET NuGet) / v1.39.3 (Python PyPI). The Agent Framework repo (microsoft/agent-framework) is actively releasing preview versions.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: multi_agent | orchestrator | graph_based | event_driven — The framework provides two complementary orchestration modes: (1) Agent Orchestration — LLM-driven, creative reasoning and decision-making for open-ended tasks, supporting patterns like sequential, concurrent, handoff, and Magentic orchestration; (2) Workflow Orchestration — business-logic driven, deterministic multi-agent workflows with graph-based routing. Graph-based architecture supports conditional routing, parallel processing, dynamic execution paths, nesting, checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop request/response patterns. Built on an asynchronous, event-driven core inherited from AutoGen v0.4's actor model.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Model-agnostic via provider abstraction — the same code works with Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Meta Llama, Mistral, local models via Ollama, Foundry Local (on-device inference), GitHub Models, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Integration packages exist for Azure AI, Anthropic, Ollama, and more. Each agent can use a different model provider. Supports both chat completion and response APIs.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Native MCP (Model Context Protocol) client support — agents dynamically discover and invoke external tools or data servers exposed over MCP without custom glue code. Also supports OpenAPI-first tool design, function calling via native decorators, plugin architecture inherited from Semantic Kernel, and direct SDK tool registration. Integration packages include Redis, Mem0, A2A, and DevUI connectors.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: Hybrid: supports both LLM-driven planning (ReAct-style reasoning through tool use in Agent Orchestration) and deterministic graph-based planning (Workflow Orchestration with explicit edges, conditional routing, and typed routing). The Magentic orchestration pattern (inherited from AutoGen's MagenticOne) uses an orchestrator agent that creates plans, delegates to specialized sub-agents, and tracks progress. The upcoming Process Framework (GA Q2 2026) adds BPMN-style deterministic business workflow orchestration with compliance audit trails.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: First-class multi-agent support with multiple orchestration patterns: Sequential (ordered agent chain), Concurrent (parallel agent execution), Handoff (context-preserving delegation between domain-expert agents — the agent decides whether to hand off or continue), Magentic (orchestrator + specialist sub-agents), and custom graph-based topologies. Agents communicate through asynchronous messages supporting both event-driven and request/response patterns. Teams can be nested. Cross-language agent communication between Python and .NET agents is supported.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (chat history via AgentSession) | semantic (long-term knowledge via vector stores) | episodic (long-term persistence of interactions across sessions via Mem0 integration) — Short-Term Memory: managed via AgentSession which stores conversation history and session state. Long-Term Memory: persists information across sessions, allowing agents to recall knowledge, preferences, and outcomes over time. Memory types are extensible via ContextProvider abstract class and custom memory implementations.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: ContextProvider abstract class allows custom logic before and after each inference call — injecting additional context, inspecting messages, and managing context windows. Supports RAG-based retrieval for surfacing relevant prior context. AgentSession handles chat history management. Custom context providers can implement summarization, truncation, or retrieval strategies. Azure AI Search integration for enterprise-scale retrieval.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: in_memory (default AgentSession) | database (Redis via integration package) | vector_store (Azure AI Search, custom vector stores) | cloud (Azure AI Foundry managed state) — AgentSession is the state abstraction; agents themselves are stateless (same agent instance can be used with multiple sessions). State serialization supported for checkpointing and resumption.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is treated as a first-class architectural concern via the ContextProvider system. ContextProviders are associated with AgentThread instances and run custom logic before and after each LLM invocation — they can inject relevant context from any source (memory stores, external databases, user profiles), inspect all messages, and modify the context window. The AIContextProvider pattern (introduced December 2025) enables contextual memory injection with sophisticated relevance filtering. The stateless agent / stateful session separation is a deliberate architectural decision enabling scalable context management.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Unified multi-agent orchestration combining Semantic Kernel's enterprise-grade features (session-based state management, type safety, middleware filters, telemetry, extensive model/embedding support) with AutoGen's innovative agent patterns (actor model, group chat, swarm, MagenticOne). Key capabilities include: (1) Individual AI agents with tool use, MCP integration, and structured output; (2) Graph-based workflows connecting multiple agents and functions for complex multi-step tasks; (3) Multiple orchestration patterns (sequential, concurrent, handoff, Magentic); (4) Middleware system for intercepting and processing agent actions; (5) Human-in-the-loop with formal approval workflows; (6) Checkpointing and resume for long-running workflows; (7) Cross-language support (Python and .NET, Java planned); (8) AutoGen Studio — low-code visual interface for prototyping agent workflows; (9) Process Framework (upcoming Q2 2026) for deterministic enterprise business process orchestration; (10) Native Azure AI Foundry integration for managed deployment, monitoring, and scaling.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code (generation + execution), web browsing (via MagenticOne WebSurfer agent), file system access (FileSurfer agent), vision (via multimodal model clients), terminal/shell execution, API calls. Primary focus is text-based reasoning and tool use with extensible modality support.
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop | supervised | fully_autonomous — Configurable per agent and workflow. Human-in-the-loop is implemented via RequestInfoEvent with formal approval workflows. Tools can be marked as requiring human approval (Agent Framework automatically emits pending approval requests routable to UI or queue). Handoff orchestration allows agents to escalate to humans. High-impact actions (database writes, financial transactions) can mandate HITL confirmation. Fully autonomous mode available for trusted workflows.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Rich and extensible. MCP client support for connecting to any MCP-compatible tool server. OpenAPI-based tool registration. Semantic Kernel plugin ecosystem (extensive library of pre-built plugins). Function calling via native decorators. Integration packages for: Azure AI services, Redis, Mem0, A2A protocol, DevUI, Anthropic, Ollama, and more. Code execution environments (Docker, local sandbox). Web browsing tools (Playwright-based via MagenticOne). Composio integration for 250+ SaaS tools. Custom tools via BaseTool class or function decoration.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Yes — first-class MCP support. Agents dynamically discover and invoke external tools or data servers exposed over MCP. Native MCP client integration for connecting to any MCP-compliant service without custom glue code. Supports both stdio (local) and HTTP (remote) MCP server connections. Agents can also be exposed as MCP servers, enabling bidirectional interoperability. Growing ecosystem of MCP-compatible services.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Yes — native Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol support via integration package. Enables cross-framework agent collaboration where agents built in different frameworks or running in different environments can discover and communicate with each other. Supports workflows where one agent retrieves data, another analyzes it, and a third validates results — even across different runtimes and organizations.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: Not explicitly documented as a built-in feature. The framework uses its own agent configuration patterns (code-based agent definition in Python/.NET, YAML configuration in AutoGen Studio). Custom ContextProviders could be built to parse and respect AGENTS.md files, but this is not a native capability. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Strong interoperability by design. MCP support enables tool sharing with any MCP-compatible framework (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, etc.). A2A protocol enables agent-to-agent communication across framework boundaries. OpenAPI-first design ensures REST-based interoperability. Azure AI Foundry provides unified observability for agents built with multiple frameworks including LangChain, LangGraph, and OpenAI Agents SDK alongside Microsoft Agent Framework. The framework's open-standards approach (MCP, A2A, OpenTelemetry) prioritizes ecosystem interoperability over vendor lock-in.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: capability_based | sandbox — Agents are granted specific tools at creation time. Microsoft Entra Agent IDs support Least Privilege principle — authentication tokens hold only the permissions necessary for the specific task. Azure Managed Identity integration for secure credential management. Tool-level permission gating: tools can be marked as requiring human approval. Middleware filters enable custom permission checks on every agent action. Enterprise deployments leverage Azure RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) for agent and resource governance.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Built-in escalation via handoff orchestration and HITL patterns. When an agent decides not to hand off to another agent, the workflow emits a RequestInfoEvent with a HandoffAgentUserRequest that requires human response to continue. Tools marked as requiring human approval automatically emit pending approval requests routable to UI or queue. High-impact actions (delete operations on production resources, database writes, financial transactions) mandate HITL digital signature. Configurable escalation thresholds per agent, tool, and workflow.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Groundedness Scoring via automated evaluation pipeline measuring whether agent answers stay within provided context (RAG) vs. hallucinating. Azure AI Content Safety integration for content filtering. Structured output enforcement via type-safe response models. Multi-agent validation patterns (one agent validates another's output). Middleware filters can intercept and validate agent responses before delivery. Azure AI Foundry evaluation tools for systematic hallucination detection and measurement.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — comprehensive audit logging. All agent decisions (Thought -> Tool Call -> Observation -> Response) logged to Azure Monitor or Application Insights for forensic review. OpenTelemetry-based tracing captures every agent action, tool invocation, and orchestration step. Azure AI Foundry dashboards provide end-to-end visibility. Actions of every agent are auditable by design. Compliance-grade audit trails for enterprise deployments.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval | post-review | confidence_threshold | always_on — Multiple patterns supported: (1) Tool-level approval gates — tools marked as requiring human approval trigger automatic pause and request routing; (2) Handoff orchestration — agents can escalate to humans while preserving context; (3) Workflow checkpoints — explicit human review points in graph-based workflows; (4) RequestInfoEvent pattern for structured human input collection; (5) Azure AI Foundry provides governance dashboards for post-review and monitoring. The Process Framework (Q2 2026) will add formal BPMN-style human task nodes.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Microsoft (corporate governance). OpenTelemetry contributions via CNCF (Cloud Native Computing Foundation). A2A protocol participation. MCP ecosystem participation. Microsoft actively contributes to open standards for agent observability and interoperability.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Implements and contributes to: MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool interoperability, A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol) for cross-framework agent communication, OpenTelemetry for standardized agent observability (Microsoft and Cisco jointly contributed agent-specific OpenTelemetry extensions), OpenAPI for REST-based tool integration. Microsoft is a driving force behind standardizing multi-agent observability through OpenTelemetry.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Enterprise-grade compliance through Azure platform: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, FedRAMP, ISO 27001, EU data residency (Azure regions). Azure AI Content Safety for content filtering and moderation. Microsoft Responsible AI principles embedded in framework guidance. Azure Entra ID for identity and access management. EU AI Act readiness through Azure's compliance infrastructure. NIST-based security governance framework for AI agents documented in Microsoft's Cloud Adoption Framework.

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: cloud | local | hybrid | edge | managed_service — (1) Azure AI Foundry Agent Service (managed cloud, GA since May 2025); (2) Self-hosted on any cloud or on-premise via Docker/Kubernetes; (3) Local development with Ollama or Foundry Local for on-device inference; (4) Hybrid: agents can span cloud and edge. The framework runs anywhere Python or .NET runs.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: horizontal | serverless — Azure AI Foundry provides serverless scaling for managed agent deployments. Self-hosted deployments support horizontal scaling via Kubernetes. The actor-model architecture (inherited from AutoGen Core) enables distributed agent networks across organizational boundaries. Azure Functions and Logic Apps integration for serverless workflows.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: The framework itself is free and open-source (MIT). Azure AI Foundry Agent Service: no additional charge for the agent service itself — you pay only for model tokens consumed and Azure tools invoked (AI Search, Bing Grounding, Logic Apps, etc.). Model costs vary by provider: GPT-4o ~$2.50/$10 per 1M input/output tokens, GPT-4o-mini ~$0.15/$0.60, local models via Ollama are free. Total cost per task depends on complexity, number of agents, and tools invoked — simple single-agent tasks can cost fractions of a cent, complex multi-agent workflows with premium models may cost $0.10-$2.00+.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Lightweight SDK — runs on standard development hardware. Python 3.10+ or .NET 8+ required. No GPU needed for cloud model inference (API-based). Local model inference via Ollama or Foundry Local requires appropriate GPU/RAM for the chosen model. Production deployments on Azure require appropriate Azure subscription and resource provisioning. Docker support for containerized deployment.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Native Azure Monitor and Application Insights integration. OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation for framework-agnostic observability. Azure AI Foundry dashboards provide unified monitoring for agents built with Microsoft Agent Framework and other frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK). Semantic Kernel telemetry (inherited) provides detailed metric and trace emission. Compatible with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Langfuse, Langsmith, Jaeger, Grafana, etc.).
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — comprehensive tracing via OpenTelemetry. Every agent action, tool invocation, orchestration step, and LLM call is traceable. Azure AI Foundry provides visual trace exploration. Microsoft and Cisco jointly contributed agent-specific OpenTelemetry extensions to standardize multi-agent tracing. Distributed tracing spans agent networks across services and organizational boundaries.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: beta (Agent Framework in public preview, GA Q1 2026) — However, the constituent components are enterprise_grade: Azure AI Foundry Agent Service has been GA since May 2025, Semantic Kernel is production-ready (v1.70.0, used by major enterprises), and AutoGen powers production workloads at scale. Microsoft states the public preview offers acceptable production risk given the battle-tested components underneath. Full enterprise readiness certification targeted at GA.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: microsoft/agent-framework: ~7.1k stars (as of Feb 2026, young repo since Oct 2025). microsoft/autogen: ~54.4k stars. microsoft/semantic-kernel: ~26.7k stars. Combined ecosystem represents one of the largest agent development communities on GitHub.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: Semantic Kernel: 26.7k GitHub stars, extensive NuGet downloads (millions), Java SDK also available. AutoGen: 54.4k GitHub stars, 559+ contributors, ~5.9k forks, active Discord community. Agent Framework (new unified repo): 7.1k stars, 1.1k forks, rapidly growing. Azure AI Foundry Agent Service (GA May 2025) serves enterprise customers globally. Major enterprises already run production workloads on these components. Microsoft's enterprise sales channel drives adoption across Fortune 500 companies.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: open-source (MIT) + managed cloud service — Framework SDK: completely free and open-source. Azure AI Foundry: platform is free to use and explore; you pay for model tokens and Azure services consumed. Azure AI Foundry Agent Service: no additional charge (pay only for underlying model and tool usage). Enterprise support available through Microsoft Azure support plans. No per-agent or per-seat licensing.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Enterprise workflow automation (multi-agent business processes with compliance trails), customer service and support orchestration (multi-agent handoff with human escalation), research and analysis pipelines (MagenticOne-style specialist agent teams), code generation and review, document processing and extraction, financial analysis, IT operations automation, supply chain optimization, healthcare and regulated industry workflows (with HIPAA/compliance support), Microsoft 365 Copilot integrations, Azure resource management and monitoring.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: The strongest enterprise play in the agent framework space. Key differentiators: (1) deepest cloud integration of any agent framework (native Azure, Entra ID, Monitor, AI Search); (2) multi-language support (Python, .NET, Java planned) — unique among major frameworks; (3) production SLAs and formal Microsoft support contracts; (4) compliance certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP) via Azure; (5) Process Framework for deterministic business workflows. Weaker than LangGraph for: cutting-edge community innovation speed, Python-first developer experience. Weaker than CrewAI for: rapid prototyping simplicity. Strongest for: enterprises already in the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem, regulated industries, and organizations needing multi-language support.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: assistant (executes with approval) | autonomous (acts independently) — Configurable per deployment. Default: autonomous within defined tool scope. With HITL approval gates: assistant mode requiring human sign-off for high-impact actions. Handoff orchestration enables dynamic switching between autonomous and supervised modes. Enterprise deployments typically operate in assistant/supervised mode with governance controls.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Built-in Handoff Orchestration pattern: an agent can either hand off to another agent (preserving full conversation context) or escalate to a human user. When escalating, the workflow emits a RequestInfoEvent with HandoffAgentUserRequest payload containing the agent's recent messages. The human must respond to continue the workflow. Azure AI Foundry can route approval requests to queues, UIs, or Teams channels. Middleware filters enable custom handoff logic at any point in the workflow. The Process Framework will add formal BPMN-style human task assignment.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Long-term memory (via Mem0 and custom ContextProviders) persists interaction outcomes across sessions, enabling agents to improve over time. Azure AI Foundry evaluation tools enable systematic assessment of agent quality (groundedness, relevance, fluency). Microsoft Responsible AI dashboards track agent performance metrics. Middleware filters allow injecting feedback signals into agent context. No built-in RLHF pipeline — improvements come through prompt refinement, memory accumulation, evaluation-driven iteration, and model fine-tuning via Azure AI Foundry.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Strong applicability for startups in the Microsoft ecosystem, but with important nuances. USE WHEN: (1) Your stack already includes Azure, .NET, or Microsoft 365 — the integration depth is unmatched; (2) You need multi-language support (e.g., .NET backend + Python ML services); (3) You are in a regulated industry (healthcare, finance, government) where compliance certifications matter; (4) You need enterprise-grade observability, audit trails, and support SLAs from day one; (5) You want a single framework that scales from prototype (AutoGen Studio) to production (Azure AI Foundry). AVOID WHEN: (1) You are a Python-only team not in the Azure ecosystem — LangGraph or CrewAI may offer a faster start; (2) You need the simplest possible multi-agent setup — CrewAI's role-based abstraction is more intuitive for non-technical founders; (3) You are cost-sensitive and want to avoid any cloud lock-in — the framework is MIT-licensed but the enterprise features lean heavily on Azure; (4) The GA timeline (Q1 2026) is a concern for production launches in early 2026 — the public preview has potential breaking changes. STARTUP ADVANTAGE: MIT license, free Azure AI Foundry platform access, and Microsoft for Startups program can offset initial costs. The unified framework means you won't outgrow your agent infrastructure as you scale.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUILD with Microsoft Agent Framework when: you have Python or .NET developers, are in the Azure ecosystem, need compliance/audit capabilities, and want a framework backed by the largest enterprise software company. The MIT license eliminates vendor lock-in at the framework level. BUY (use Azure AI Foundry Agent Service) when: you want managed deployment, scaling, and monitoring without DevOps overhead — and the pay-per-token model keeps costs proportional to usage. ALTERNATIVES: LangGraph for maximum Python-native control and graph-based state management, CrewAI for simplest multi-agent role-play abstraction, OpenAI Agents SDK if deeply committed to the OpenAI model ecosystem. Cost comparison: Microsoft Agent Framework + GPT-4o-mini via Azure is cost-competitive with all alternatives, and Azure AI Foundry Agent Service adds no markup over raw model costs.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 4 (AI business models & strategy) — exemplifies the open-source-plus-cloud-managed-service business model (framework free, cloud services monetized). Also relevant to Session 3 (AI project framing — Build vs Buy, framework selection, enterprise integration patterns) and Session 5 (governance, compliance, EU AI Act readiness through Azure infrastructure, multi-agent safety and audit trails).

confidence.data_quality: High — based on official Microsoft documentation (learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework), Microsoft Azure blog, Microsoft Foundry blog, Microsoft Research publications, GitHub repository data (microsoft/agent-framework, microsoft/autogen, microsoft/semantic-kernel), Visual Studio Magazine, InfoQ, European AI & Cloud Summit analysis, and Azure pricing pages.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub confirms 7.1k stars for microsoft/agent-framework, MIT license. AutoGen 54.4k stars and Semantic Kernel 26.7k stars confirmed via GitHub. October 2025 public preview date confirmed by multiple sources (Microsoft Azure Blog, Visual Studio Magazine, InfoQ). GA Q1 2026 target confirmed by European AI & Cloud Summit analysis and Microsoft community posts. MCP and A2A support confirmed by official documentation and Azure blog. Azure AI Foundry Agent Service GA (May 2025) confirmed by Azure pricing page.
confidence.caveats: The Agent Framework is in public preview as of February 2026 — APIs may have breaking changes before GA. The GA 1.0 target of Q1 2026 is a stated goal, not a guarantee. The relationship between the new microsoft/agent-framework repo and the existing microsoft/semantic-kernel and microsoft/autogen repos is still evolving — Semantic Kernel and AutoGen will remain supported but investment is shifting to Agent Framework. The Process Framework (deterministic business workflows) is not yet available (GA Q2 2026). Some enterprise features are tightly coupled to Azure, which may concern multi-cloud or cloud-agnostic organizations. Community is split across three GitHub repos which can be confusing for newcomers. The 7.1k stars for the unified repo is modest compared to competitors like CrewAI (43k+) and LangGraph, though the combined AutoGen+SK ecosystem is much larger.
